on_screen: Your users already live in Snowflake or BigQuery, with attributes like country, age band, plan, device and app version.
Your own SQL query picks the eligible users and the attributes your targeting rules need.
A short sync script you write sends them in chunks of up to 1,000 users to POST /api/v1/tracking/assign/batch (beta), each user's attributes as context, with an API key.
60 requests a minute per address. Over that, the API answers 429 with Retry-After; wait and resend. Resending is safe because assignments are sticky.
The experiment's targeting rules admit some users. The rest get assigned: false, reason: "targeting": they see the control and nothing is recorded.
Admitted users are split by a deterministic hash: the same user always lands in the same bucket, and an assigned user keeps their variant.
The response lists every user in request order, with counts for each reason. Enrolled users count in results from the moment they are assigned.
The experiment is in the dashboard. When a user arrives, the SDK's assign call returns the same variant and records the view.
